cases.title: Streamline Carports
cases.excerpt: Streamline Carports builds steel carports for Auckland homeowners. A refined Meta audience and durability-led creative cut its cost per lead by 62% while enquiries grew tenfold.
cases.description: How Digilari cut Streamline Carports' Meta cost per lead by 62% and grew enquiries from about 2 to about 20 a month.
cases.subtitle: Cutting the Cost of Every Quote Request with Meta Lead Ads
cases.about: Streamline Carports designs and builds steel carports for homeowners across Auckland, with sustainable PurlinDek steel roofing and a 10-year structural warranty. Meta Ads is one of its main sources of quote requests, sending people to the carports page to request a quote or get in touch.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Steel carports
Location
Auckland, New Zealand
Channels
Facebook and Instagram (Meta Ads)
Objective
Quote and contact enquiries
Period
May 2024 to October 2026
cases.challenge_html:
Streamline needed a steady flow of quote requests from Meta at a cost that made sense for a considered home purchase.

At launch (May to October 2024), a broad Auckland campaign was costing NZ$148 per enquiry and bringing in about 2 enquiries a month. The audience was too wide, and the creative wasn't giving homeowners a clear reason to choose Streamline over a cheaper alternative.
cases.challenge_caption: Top ad (Carports | Oct 2025 | Ad 2): 156 leads at NZ$52.40 each over the last 12 months
cases.solutions_intro: Digilari rebuilt the audience and creative, then kept moving budget towards what the results supported:

boxes.title: Refined lookalike audience
boxes.description:
• Built an ad set from a 1% lookalike of recent website visitors, layered with homeowner, home improvement and vehicle-owner interests.
  • Run side by side with the original broad audience, it cost 42% less per lead (NZ$61.44 against NZ$105.49).

boxes.title: Durability-led creative
boxes.description:
• Rebuilt the ads around what matters to carport buyers: strength, rust protection, PurlinDek steel roofing and a 10-year structural warranty.
  • Meta's flexible format tested three images with several headlines and primary texts in each ad.

boxes.title: Budget that follows results
boxes.description:
• Paused the weaker broad ad set and moved its budget to the refined one.
  • When GA4 showed a separate traffic campaign's visitors weren't engaging, 70% of its budget moved into lead generation.

boxes.title: Creative fatigue monitoring
boxes.description: • Tracked cost per lead month by month and refreshed copy and creative when results slipped, rather than letting ageing ads absorb more budget.

results.title: Lower Cost per Lead, Ten Times the Enquiries
results.editor:
1. Cost per lead:
    • Down 62%, from NZ$148.22 at launch to NZ$56.57 over the last 12 months.
  2. Lead volume:
    • From about 2 enquiries a month at launch to about 20 a month, with 234 Meta-reported leads in the last 12 months.
  3. Click efficiency:
    • Click-through rate up from 1.14% to 1.56%, and cost per click down from NZ$1.09 to NZ$0.82.
  4. Website activity:
    • GA4 recorded 80 quote and contact form submissions and 54 phone-link clicks from Meta visitors over the same 12 months.

cases.title: CV Sheds
cases.excerpt: CV Sheds builds custom steel sheds across Central Victoria. A seasonal Meta series with tight local targeting brought in more relevant visitors at a 41% lower cost per click.
cases.description: How a seasonal Meta campaign for CV Sheds lifted click-through rate by 49% and cut cost per click by 41% across Central Victoria.
cases.subtitle: A Seasonal Meta Campaign That Reaches Shed Buyers Before the Busy Season
cases.about: CV Sheds designs and builds custom steel sheds across Central Victoria. Google Ads captures people already searching for a shed. Meta's job is different: reach property owners earlier and bring them to the website before the busy summer build season.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Custom steel sheds
Location
Central Victoria
Channels
Facebook and Instagram (Meta Ads)
Objective
Website visits ahead of the build season
Period
February to November 2026
cases.challenge_html:
The client's brief was a single line: plan a January campaign along the lines of “New Year, New Shed”, with the concept left to Digilari.

The campaign needed to bring low-cost, relevant visitors to the site from the right towns, without spending on Melbourne or audiences unlikely to build a shed. The New Year's campaign finished at a 1.85% click-through rate and $0.44 per landing page view.
cases.challenge_caption: Summer Campaign single image ad: 3.12% click-through rate at $0.18 per click
cases.solutions_intro: Digilari turned the brief into a seasonal series and tightened every part of the targeting:

boxes.title: A seasonal campaign series
boxes.description:
• New Year's ran in three creative phases from February to May 2026.
  • Summer Campaign 2026 followed in August with the same “prepare before the season” angle: protect vehicles, machinery, boats and caravans from summer sun and storms.

boxes.title: Local targeting around 22 towns
boxes.description:
• Ads reached people within 25 miles of 22 Central Victorian towns, including Bendigo, Ballarat, Castlemaine and Echuca, with Melbourne excluded.
  • Interests matched shed buyers: farming and machinery, boating, caravans and 4WD, DIY and home improvement, plus the Recently moved life event.

boxes.title: Three formats tested
boxes.description:
• Single image, carousel and video ads launched side by side.
  • The single image won clearly (3.12% click-through rate at $0.18 per click), and Meta put 81% of September's budget behind it.

boxes.title: Cleaner placements and tracking
boxes.description: • Audience Network placements were excluded, Advantage+ creative enhancements were switched on, and UTM parameters were standardised so GA4 attributes Meta visits correctly.

results.title: Cheaper, More Relevant Visits Ahead of Summer
results.editor:
1. Click-through rate:
    • 2.75%, against 1.85% on the previous seasonal campaign.
  2. Cost per click:
    • $0.22, down from $0.37.
  3. Cost per landing page view:
    • $0.37, down from $0.44, across 2,190 landing page views.
  4. Best month:
    • September 2026, at a 3.63% click-through rate, $0.16 per click and $0.30 per landing page view.

cases.extra_html:

cases.title: Cummins
cases.excerpt: Cummins had no established social presence in the Philippines. Digilari built an industry-focused Facebook programme that educated buyers, supported the local sales team and stayed on brand.
cases.description: How Digilari built and managed an industry-focused Facebook presence for Cummins Power Generation in the Philippines.
cases.subtitle: Building a Social Presence for a Global Power Brand in the Philippines
cases.about: Cummins is a global power technology company. Its Philippine power generation team needed a Facebook presence that would introduce Cummins gensets to the businesses that rely on dependable power and support the local sales team's priorities.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Power generation
Market
Philippines
Channel
Facebook (organic)
Focus
Brand awareness, product education and sales support
cases.challenge_html:
Cummins didn't have an established social media presence in the Philippines. It wanted to build brand awareness across key industries, particularly commercial, data centre and healthcare, while also supporting its sales efforts.

Creative freedom was limited by established global brand templates and guidelines, so the content had to stand out through its topics and relevance rather than a new look.
cases.challenge_caption: Illustration based on the campaign messaging
cases.solutions_intro: Digilari built a content programme around the industries that buy gensets and refined it with data:

boxes.title: Industry-specific content streams
boxes.description:
• Content started with commercial businesses such as petrol stations, fast-food franchises, banks, malls and supermarkets, plus agricultural businesses that need power for irrigation, aerators and ventilation.
  • Data centres and healthcare facilities were added as the programme grew.

boxes.title: Education alongside product
boxes.description:
• Posts explained topics such as the difference between a Cummins Power Generation genset and an OEM genset powered by Cummins.
  • Value-added, educational content ran alongside product and sales posts, so the page never felt like a sales pitch.

boxes.title: A data-led posting schedule
boxes.description:
• Daily single-image posts first established when target audiences were most active.
  • Content topics were then tested against publishing days over three months, setting the posting schedule and message exposure for the following quarters.

boxes.title: Formats that kept pace with the platform
boxes.description: • Reels were introduced as Meta began favouring video, keeping the content fresh and reducing creative fatigue while staying within Cummins' brand guidelines.

results.title: A Consistent, Industry-Focused Presence the Local Team Valued
results.editor:
1. New presence:
    • Established and managed Cummins Power Generation's Facebook presence in the Philippines.
  2. Wider reach into industry:
    • Content expanded from general awareness to commercial, agricultural, data centre and healthcare audiences.
  3. A tested schedule:
    • A structured, data-backed posting schedule used through to the end of the engagement.
  4. Client feedback:
    • The Philippine team reported being happy with the campaign throughout, with no requests to change direction.

cases.extra_html:
Results are based on campaign management records and client feedback.

cases.title: Cosmetics Plus
cases.excerpt: Cosmetics Plus had duplicate Facebook pages and a backlog of negative reviews. Digilari consolidated its presence, set up a review process and built content that kept local stores top of mind.
cases.description: How Digilari consolidated Cosmetics Plus' Facebook pages, managed its reputation and grew engagement on Facebook and Instagram.
cases.subtitle: Cleaning Up and Growing a Beauty Retailer's Social Presence
cases.about: Cosmetics Plus is a beauty retailer offering cosmetics, self-care products and in-store piercing services through its local stores. Social media supports both its online reputation and foot traffic to each store.
cases.facts_html:
Industry
Beauty and piercing retail
Channels
Facebook and Instagram, with Pinterest maintained
Focus
Community management, reputation and local store visits
cases.challenge_html:
When Cosmetics Plus came on board it had very little social media presence. Its Facebook page was largely inactive, and there were several duplicate pages and negative reviews that needed attention.

Before the brand could grow online, its digital footprint had to be cleaned up, its pages consolidated and its customer feedback addressed.
cases.challenge_caption: Illustration based on the campaign messaging
cases.solutions_intro: Digilari fixed the foundations first, then built a content programme on top of them:

boxes.title: Page clean-up and consolidation
boxes.description: • Claimed the duplicate and existing public business pages and consolidated them into one official Facebook page.

boxes.title: Reputation management
boxes.description: • Responded to the backlog of reviews and complaints, de-escalated where possible, and wrote a standard process for answering every type of review, from positive feedback to complaints.

boxes.title: Consistent community replies
boxes.description: • Created scripts for frequently asked questions and repeat enquiries, so replies stayed consistent across platforms before chatbots were widely available.

boxes.title: Content beyond promotions
boxes.description:
• Aligned social content with the promotional calendar, then filled the gaps with self-care tips, piercing education and product features.
  • Reels moved from slideshows to creative videos with transitions, movement and music.

boxes.title: Focused channels and local promotion
boxes.description:
• Narrowed active posting from Facebook, Instagram, X and Pinterest to Facebook and Instagram, while keeping Pinterest boards up to date.
  • Paid piercing promotions reached people within 20 km of each store.

results.title: One Official Page, a Clear Process and More Engaging Content
results.editor:
1. Consolidated presence:
    • Duplicate pages resolved into one official Facebook page.
  2. Reputation:
    • The backlog of reviews and complaints answered, with a documented process for handling feedback from then on.
  3. Community management:
    • Consistent, scripted replies to common questions across platforms.
  4. Content:
    • Reworked Reels performed well with the algorithm and increased reach and impressions.

cases.extra_html:
Results are based on campaign management records.
